mission_08: The Law of Large Numbers states that as the number of trials increases, the sample average converges to the expected value. The weak law says convergence in probability; the strong law says almost sure convergence. Chebyshev's inequality provides a bound: P(|X_bar - mu| >= epsilon) <= Var(X)/(n*epsilon^2), showing that the probability of deviation decreases as 1/n. This theorem justifies using sample averages to estimate population parameters and is the foundation of Monte Carlo methods. In ML, the LLN justifies using empirical risk (training loss) as an estimate of true risk (expected loss).
